anomalies.observed: For channel 1, both 0 Ω jumpers R19 (J3.19 to /NET0011) and R8 (J3.21 to /NET0011) are populated, so bus pins 19 and 21 are shorted together. For channel 2, both R14 (J3.20) and R16 (J3.22) tie to /NET0042, shorting pins 20 and 22 together.
anomalies.expected: The spec describes R9–R12 as a select pair per channel: one jumper of each pair is shorted to choose the bus pin (19 or 21 for ch.1, 20 or 22 for ch.2). Shorting both pins of a pair ties two M5Stack GPIOs together and drives them from one PWM line.

evidence.quote: R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2

anomalies.impact: Two GPIOs from the M5Stack bus are shorted together. Depending on the pins, this can create contention or drive a bus-level conflict (for example, I2C lines), and it can disturb the servo PWM signal.

anomalies.observed: MAX3485 pin 7 (B) connects only to the R10/R22 bias divider. It is not connected to the servo bus, while the A line (U2.6, /NET0016) is the one tied to the bus through R1.
anomalies.expected: For a single-wire half-duplex TTL bus, the transceiver's differential pair should be connected to the bus consistently, with A and B both on the bus or B at a defined bias level as the design intends.

evidence.quote: Serial mode: the two servo signal pins are bridged into one shared half-duplex TTL serial bus, driven through a MAX3485

anomalies.impact: The serial bus is driven and received on A only, with B biased at a mid-level by a 2.2 kΩ divider. Communication may work but with reduced noise margin and an unbalanced, nonstandard topology.

parsed.summary: The netlist is mostly consistent with the spec, but the 0 Ω jumper pattern shorts two bus GPIO pins together for each servo channel. That contradicts the spec's one-jumper-per-channel selection, so this is the most likely anomaly, with lower confidence.
